tutor.en: Hello! What can we get you?

options.sk: Dobrý deň. Chcem zeleninu na polievku.
Dobrý deň. Ja chcieť zeleninu na polievku.
options.why: Slovak needs the conjugated verb: 'chcem' (I want), not the infinitive 'chcieť'.

options.sk: Dobrý deň. Chcem zeleninom na polievku.
options.why: 'Zeleninu' is the accusative object; 'zeleninom' is instrumental.

tutor.sk: Máme zemiaky, cibuľu a papriku. Čo ešte?
tutor.en: We have potatoes, onions and peppers. What else?

options.why: Both objects are accusative: 'zemiaky a cibuľu'; 'cibuľom' is instrumental.
You are buying several: the plural accusative 'zemiaky'; 'zemiak a cibuľa' only names the things.

tutor.en: How many potatoes do you want?

options.why: After 'kilo' the genitive plural follows: 'kilo zemiakov', not 'zemiaky'.
'Zemiakoch' is the locative; the weight takes the genitive: 'kilo zemiakov'.

tutor.sk: Ešte niečo? Paprika je dnes pekná.
tutor.en: Anything else? The peppers are nice today.

options.sk: Áno, dajte mi aj tri papriky.
Áno, dajte mi aj tri paprika.
options.why: With three the noun is plural: 'tri papriky', not the singular 'paprika'.

options.sk: Áno, dá mi aj tri papriky.
options.why: 'Dajte' is the polite request to you; 'dá' means he or she gives.
You want the bag — accusative: 'tašku', not the naming form 'taška'.
'Taškou' is instrumental; what you want is the accusative 'tašku'.

tutor.sk: Tak to je za všetko tri eurá a pol.
tutor.en: So that is three euros fifty for everything.

options.why: Paying IN cash is instrumental: 'hotovosťou'; 'hotovosti' is the locative.
You need the conjugated 'zaplatím' (I will pay), not the infinitive 'platiť'.
On leaving you say 'dovidenia'; 'dobrý deň' is the greeting.
The Slovak word is 'ďakujem', written with ď.
